This document is historical. The old 2024 process promoted any model when accuracy exceeded 0.80. It is superseded by release-policy: current releases use F1 and ROC-AUC on a frozen holdout. Do not apply the old rule.

Production model changes require an evaluation on a frozen holdout. Promote only when F1 improves by at least 0.005 and ROC-AUC drops by no more than 0.01. A drift alert alone never authorizes promotion. Keep the previous production version for rollback. The release approver is the project owner.

answer.answer: No, the old memo is not enough. The legacy 2024 memo promoted any model when accuracy exceeded 0.80, so a model with accuracy 0.82 would have qualified under that rule. However, that memo is explicitly superseded by the current release policy, which no longer uses accuracy. Under the current governing policy, promotion requires an evaluation on a frozen holdout and is allowed only when F1 improves by at least 0.005 and ROC-AUC drops by no more than 0.01; a drift alert alone never authorizes promotion, the previous production version must be kept for rollback, and the release approver is the project owner. Since this model has worse F1 (not an improvement of at least 0.005), it does not meet the current promotion criteria, and the old accuracy-based rule must not be applied.
